Two circles of radius 7 cm and 5 cm intersect each other at A and B, and the
distance between their centres is 10 cm, the length of the common chord AB is:
If arcs of equal length in two circles subtend angles of 40° and 50° at their centers, then the ratio of their radii is:
solutionText: Arc length l = rθ. Since the arcs are equal, r₁θ₁ = r₂θ₂. Therefore r₁/r₂ = θ₂/θ₁ = 50/40 = 5/4. Hence the ratio of radii is 5:4. Link: https://youtu.be/UNklq50VFbY?t=528

questionText: From a point P outside a circle, a tangent PA and a secant PBC are drawn. If PA = 12 cm and BC = 10 cm, what is the length of the segment PB?
solutionText: By the tangent-secant theorem, PA² = PB × PC. Since PC = PB + BC, 144 = PB(PB + 10). Therefore PB² + 10PB - 144 = 0, giving PB = 8 cm. EXP: https://youtu.be/9TozM1cVe0M?t=2650

questionText: Two parallel chords on the same side of the centre of a circle are 16 cm and 30 cm long. If the distance between the two chords is 7 cm, find the radius of the circle.
solutionText: For a chord of length 30 cm, half-chord = 15 cm. For the chord of length 16 cm, half-chord = 8 cm. Let distances from centre be x and y. Since the chords are on the same side, y - x = 7. Also r² = 15² + x² = 8² + y². Thus 225 + x² = 64 + (x+7)², giving x = 7. Hence r² = 225 + 49 = 274, so r = √274 ≈ 16.55 cm. Therefore none of the listed integer options is exact.
